timecoded_text_to_speech.text: Hi, this is Randy and Kim at Family Tent Camping and we want to talk to you a little bit about the blue screw.
That one is orange, it's an OZ-10 edition, but they come in blue or orange.
Short ones are for grass and ruddy areas and we want to show you how we like to anchor down the jet tent.
Now we've used the steel stakes that come with it to anchor down the four feet around the tent,
but we like to use the blue screw to screw into the ground and anchor the guy ropes on our tent.
And so Randy's just going to screw that in.
Each one of the short ones is the equivalent of a 250 pound block of cement or anchor.
It's made out of a military grade plastic.
The only way to break when it's to bend it completely in half, it'll shatter if you do that.
But when you screw it into the ground, you want to screw down as far as you can by hand, don't need any tools.
But you can step on that thing, you can run over it with a car, you can do just about anything with it.
And it won't break because you can't bend it in half when it's in the ground.
Now we like to take the guy ropes that run from the window, from the tent itself, and from the fly of the jet tent.
All three of those, rather than putting in different stakes for each one, we run it just underneath of the tee.
So now the hole in the middle is for a D-ring shackle, or you have the hook as well, which would be for like a spring, like an awning on an RV or something like that.
But we run underneath of the tee that goes all the way up, and then you just anchor it into place.
So he's going to do the one that runs from the tent now, we're running it on the same anchor.
So you're not using a ton of them, just four.
All the way around the tent, one in each corner.
Here's your window, the gusseted side window of the tent.
We're going to anchor that down to there as well.
Let's hook it up.
And there you have it.
You've got all three of your guy ropes for the jet tent connected to one ground anchor, which is the blue screw and blue or orange, underneath the tee handle.
And there you go, you can go off and have a good time and not worry about your tent moving anywhere, no matter what blows in.
You can find the blue screw ground anchors in large or small, the jet tent, and any other Oz tent gear or accessory at FamilyTentCamping.com.

youtube_description: The Bluescrew ground anchors (available in blue or orange) can easily take the place of individual stake out points by anchoring multiple guy ropes! See more at www.FamilyTentCamping.com
